text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate, cautious and well grounded. Its numbers match the card: 50.9% of 962 claims, expected 5.6%, score 20.58, z 7.25, and 21 documented claims. It correctly reports 0 of 9 documented 99215s below the billed level against 14% for peers. It also gets the 0 of 19 data-reviewed figure right. It balances the high statistical elevation against documentation that supports the billed level, and it says plainly that zero mismatches does not clear the provider. The cited low-complexity claims do carry the simple-visit diagnoses the text attributes to them. The weaknesses are a few unsupported or imprecise claims and next steps that are thin relative to the narrative.","problems":["The 'roughly ten times the all-provider rate even among zero or one chronic condition' claim is only loosely supported: the card shows 0.247 vs 0.022 (about 11x) and 0.35 vs 0.034 (about 10x), so it is acceptable but not stated with numbers.","The '19% low complexity' figure is rounded from 0.188; this is fine, and the number-check flag on '99215' is just the CPT code, not a real discrepancy.","The 'about one mismatch' expectation is derived from 14% of 9, which is about 1.3. It is a reasonable inference but is not shown on the card.","The narrative recommends requesting charts for the specific low-complexity 99215s (Z09, URI, back pain), but the coded next_steps are generic ('larger sample of 99214 and 99215') and do not name those claims.","The cited_claim_ids list only two claims (C0073928, C0073955). These are the weakest examples, with real chronic conditions like hypertension and atrial fibrillation, rather than the stronger Z09 or zero-condition cases the text relies on.","The 'billing almost entirely 99214/99215 with few lower codes' point is true (908 of 962) but has no numbers.","The summary does not flag that one supported 99215 (C0074143) has no recorded minutes, though minutes are not essential."]}
